newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shekel rises against dollar.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shekel rises against dollar.

text.p: The Israeli shekel rose slightly against the dollar on Tuesday and closed almost unchanged against the basket of key foreign currencies in active trading, dealers said.
The shekel fluctuates in a trading band of seven percent above or below a sloping mid-point designed to devalue the currency at a rate of six percent a year against the basket of key currencies.

"The basket was stable today, but the business sector continues to take foreign currency-linked loans. The basket is now at 6.8 percent below the diagonal rate. I believe that the Bank of Israel will not intervene before it reaches the lower edge of the band," Israel Sapir at Bank Leumi said.

The representative rate for the dollar was fixed at 3.2440 shekels against 3.2470 shekels on Monday. The basket, composed of the dollar, mark, pound sterling, French franc and yen, was fixed at 3.6193 shekels against 3.6187 on Monday.
On the crosses the shekel traded against the yen at 2.8099 shekels per 100 yen against 2.8006 on Monday and against the mark at 2.0766 shekels against 2.0722 on Monday.
In late afternoon the dollar was trading at 3.2425 shekels.
